_note: Tutorials for the craft benches. The same rules as table.json's note. The minigames' own first cards (33-bench-games.js) are not here: they keep their own words and their own rule (shown until you score well), and only their seen marks live in the tutorials store.

steps.title: Methods
steps.words: The methods of the craft run along the top, and the number keys pick them too. A locked method opens at a higher herbalism level, and says which.

steps.title: Your satchel
steps.words: On the left is what you carry that this method can work. Drag an ingredient onto the tool, click it, or press Enter on it. Anything that cannot go on the tool says why.

steps.title: Roll Craft
steps.words: Roll Craft throws your Craft check. On a success a short game plays, and how well you play sets the quality, up to the best your herbalism level allows. The column on the right shows that ladder.

steps.title: Long work
steps.words: A step of {herb_in_progress_hours} hour or longer goes In progress. You carry it with you, and it finishes in its own time while you play.

buttons.label: Recipes
buttons.words: Steps you saved, to run again.

buttons.label: Herbarium
buttons.words: What you know of each herb, in the Journal.

buttons.label: Manuals
buttons.words: Read a herbal manual you carry; reading takes hours.

buttons.label: perks to pick
buttons.words: Past the top level, each level gives perks to choose.

buttons.label: Steady mode
buttons.words: Slower games, and every hold becomes a press.

buttons.label: Close
buttons.words: Back to the table. Esc does the same.

steps.title: Methods
steps.words: The steps of smithing run along the top, and the number keys pick them too. A locked step says what opens it: a higher Blacksmith level, or a smithy's furnace, which a field kit does not have.

steps.title: Your rack
steps.words: On the left is what you carry that the forge can work: ore, bars, fuel and fittings. Drag one into the work order, or press Enter on it. A material's card holds Assay, which tests it to learn what it does.

steps.title: The work order
steps.words: On the right are the slots this step needs and, for Forge, the shape to make, with its bars and its DC. The paper tag under them shows the best quality your level allows.

steps.title: Roll Craft
steps.words: Roll Craft throws your Craft check against the DC shown. On a success a short game at the anvil sets the quality. A bad miss ruins half of what was on the anvil, the cheaper things first.

steps.title: Long work
steps.words: A step of {forge_in_progress_hours} hour or longer goes In progress. Worked at a smithy it waits there for you to collect; worked from a field kit, you carry it. The line at the foot says where you are working.

buttons.label: Manuals
buttons.words: Read a smithing manual you carry.

buttons.label: Close
buttons.words: Back to the table; Esc too.

steps.title: Three steps in order
steps.words: Prepare lays a circle round a vessel, Attune seats essences on it, and Bind makes it magic. Read, Identify and Unbind work beside them. The number keys pick a method; a locked one says the level that opens it.

steps.title: Your shelf
steps.words: On the left are the vessels, circle materials and essences you carry, each essence with its motes. Drag one into the working, or press Enter on it. A worn or held item cannot go in the circle: take it off first.

steps.title: The working
steps.words: On the right is the working: the vessel, the circle's line, ink and treatment, then the seats the essences sit in. It shows the DC and what makes it up, and the paper tag shows your quality ceiling.

steps.title: The roll
steps.words: Under the circle you are told what a miss would cost before you roll. On a success a short game sets the step's quality. Each essence family has its hour of the day: bind inside it and the game's windows are wider.

steps.title: Binding takes days
steps.words: A Bind that lands goes In progress for the book's time, and you need not stand over it. Stop it early and the item comes back as it was, but the essences are spent.

steps.title: Buttons along the foot
steps.words: Close, or Esc, goes back to the table.

buttons.label: Manuals
buttons.words: Read an enchanting manual you carry.

steps.title: Methods
steps.words: The methods run along the top, and the number keys pick them too. Most work starts with Dissolve and ends with Bottle, and a bottled product never goes back in. A locked method says the level that opens it.

steps.title: Your shelf
steps.words: On the left are the reagents, solvents and vessels you carry. Drag one onto the formula card, or press Enter on it. The ? beside a reagent opens its card: what you know of it, and Assay to learn more.

steps.title: The formula card
steps.words: On the right: what goes in, the vessel, the formula or Experiment, and the traits it will carry. Bottle with no formula chosen and you experiment; a mix that fits one formula within your reach is written into your Formulary.

steps.title: Roll Craft
steps.words: The mishap a miss would bring is said under the glass before you roll. On a success a short game sets the quality, up to the ceiling on the paper tag. Distill, Sublime, Transmute and rare reagents need a laboratory.

steps.title: Long work
steps.words: A step longer than {alchemy_in_progress_hours} hours, and every Transmute, goes In progress. You need not stand over it: it is ready when the clock reaches its time, and the line at the foot says where you are working.

steps.title: Buttons along the foot
steps.words: Close, or Esc, goes back to the table.

buttons.label: Manuals
buttons.words: Read an alchemy manual you carry.

steps.title: From hide to piece
steps.words: The steps from a green hide to a finished piece run along the top: flense, tan, cut, stitch and assemble, and more as you level. The number keys pick them too. A locked step says the level that opens it.

steps.title: Your rack
steps.words: On the left is what you carry: green hides first, each with its grade and how long before it spoils. Salt or tan a green hide in time. Drag anything into the work order, or press Enter on it.

steps.title: The work order
steps.words: On the right are the slots this step needs and the paper tag. The worst hide grade on the bench caps the quality, and the tag shows that ceiling before you roll. Green hides come from Harvest the carcass, in Craft action.

steps.title: Roll Craft
steps.words: Roll Craft throws your Craft check against the DC shown. On a success a short game at the beam sets the quality. A bad miss ruins half of what was on the bench.

steps.title: Tanning takes days
steps.words: A tanning that soaks goes In progress: in your pack, or in a tannery's vat if begun there. The line at the foot says where you are working, and what a tannery charges.

buttons.label: Ledger
buttons.words: Every hide and supply you have met.

buttons.label: Close
buttons.words: Back to the table; Esc too.

steps.title: A short game after the roll
steps.words: After a good roll at any bench a short game plays, and how well you play sets the quality. Each game shows its own first card until you play it well, and the ? on the game's strip pauses it.

steps.title: Steady mode
steps.words: Steady mode, at the foot of every bench, slows every game and turns every hold into a press. It is the same switch as Steady mode in Settings, under Sound and motion.

steps.title: Levels that never stop
steps.words: Past level {perk_from_level} a craft keeps levelling, and each level gives {perk_picks} picks from its perks; the same perk may be picked twice. Each choice says what it will do at your next pick.

buttons.label: Later
buttons.words: Keeps the picks banked; perks to pick at the foot opens this again.

buttons.label: Clear
buttons.words: Takes back the picks made so far.

buttons.label: Confirm
buttons.words: Takes the picks; they count from your next step.

steps.title: Long work, every craft
steps.words: Work from every bench that takes a long while waits here: what is ready to collect first, then what is still working, soonest first. The countdown runs on the story's clock, so it moves only as time passes in the game.

steps.title: Where it opens
steps.words: In progress opens this panel from under the bench doors on the left side, and from the foot of every bench. The count beside it says how many are ready.

buttons.label: Collect
buttons.words: Takes finished work into your pack, or says why not from here.

buttons.label: Wait for it
buttons.words: Lets time pass until the work is ready.

buttons.label: Stop
buttons.words: Ends the work early; it says first what you lose.

buttons.label: Close
buttons.words: Folds the panel away. Esc does the same.

steps.title: Every craft at once
steps.words: This sheet lists what you can take from this body for every craft you have, grouped by craft. Each row says the check it takes, what comes off and how long it takes.

steps.title: Take
steps.words: Take rolls for that one part. The first part off a dangerous body faces its dangers first, a die for each, and the danger is said before you roll. A hide is then cut off in a short game that sets its grade.

steps.title: Salt and deeds
steps.words: A green hide spoils unless it is salted or tanned, and its row says whether you carry enough curing salt. Taking from a good outsider or a good dragon is a deed, and you are asked first.

buttons.label: Close
buttons.words: Back to the table; Esc too.

steps.title: One tab a craft
steps.words: Each tab is one craft, with your level in it, or not yet. The benches stand at the table now, so each tab is one card with one button: it takes you to the table with that bench open.

steps.title: Time at a bench
steps.words: A bench works in the scene where your character stands, and each step takes its time on the story's clock.

buttons.label: back to the table
buttons.words: Back to your game, as you left it.

buttons.label: worlds & characters
buttons.words: Back to the shelf of worlds and characters.
